Chapter 9: Praying the Bible in Community—Group and Family Applications
So far, we’ve spent a lot of time exploring how to pray the Bible on your own. But let’s be honest—something really special happens when you open up this practice to a group or family setting. Sharing the experience with others? It brings out new insights, encouragement, and a real sense of connection.
Wondering how to get started? Here are a few simple ways you can pray Scripture together:
First, try the shared reading and response approach. One person reads a passage out loud, and then everyone gets a chance to pray, each in their own way, letting the words spark their prayers.
Another idea is responsive prayer. After each verse or section, pause. You might sit in silence or invite spoken prayers, making room for different voices and perspectives to shine through.
Feeling creative? Encourage folks to respond to the text with a song, a piece of art, or maybe some journaling. Then, share those reflections with the group. It’s amazing how these different expressions can open up fresh conversations.
When you do this together, it builds unity. Everyone brings their own stories and insights, which makes the experience richer and the relationships deeper.
Now, if you’re thinking about families—praying the Bible together can actually become a treasured tradition. Even young kids can join in by listening, repeating simple prayers, or sharing what stood out to them. There’s no right or wrong way: keep it as structured or as relaxed as you like, and let it fit the ages and personalities in your family.
Over time, these shared moments create a real foundation of spiritual closeness and support. The words of Scripture start to become your shared language—shaping your values, your hopes, and the prayers of everyone in your community.
So, why not give it a try? You might be surprised by how much it brings you together.
